chapter: Blue Note, The Connection and Tony Williams
title: Authenticity of the play and McLean's acting
summary: He saw the play as about waiting for the connection, introducing him to theater, and he added lines.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did you feel the play was an authentic representation of what being an addict was?
Stretched, made for enjoyment, yeah, but it was about that, waiting for the connection to come, because you got something that you need.
It’s been compared to a Waiting for Godot kind of . . .
Something like that. That’s true. They did a lot of Bertolt Brecht and other plays that – I really got introduced to theater through my experience with The Connection.
How much did the piece mutate, in a sense, over time, by your involvement and the involvement of the other musicians?

It depends on who was there at the time. Freddie Redd didn’t do a lot of adding to the lines and stuff like that. I did, because I like acting and all that. I would try to get into it, sometimes when I wasn’t even supposed to. They had to sometimes, “Lighten up, man.”
